number.why: The served serious-adverse-event counts are 38/250 for tocilizumab and 25/127 for placebo, through day 60 in the safety population grouped by actual treatment received. The ruling correctly identifies the incorrect modified-intention-to-treat label. These counts confirm the served harm outcome, not 28-day mortality. The source reports counts and percentages rather than a published OR or corresponding CI.

quotes.span: In the safety population, serious adverse events occurred in 38 of 250 patients (15.2%) in the tocilizumab group and 25 of 127 patients (19.7%) in the placebo group.
Safety was assessed in all the patients who received either tocilizumab or placebo; patients were grouped according to the actual agent received.

entry.why: Eligibility explicitly establishes hospitalized adults with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia. The hypoxemia requirement and ventilation exclusions narrow the enrolled population within the question's population; they do not undermine entry eligibility.

quotes.span: Patients who were 18 years of age or older (with no upper age limit) and who were hospitalized with Covid-19 pneumonia that had been confirmed by a positive polymerase-chain-reaction test and radiographic imaging were eligible for enrollment.

Patients had a blood oxygen saturation below 94% while breathing ambient air but were excluded if they were receiving continuous positive airway pressure, bilevel positive airway pressure, or mechanical ventilation.

missed: No additional finding changes either ruling. The served row's composite-endpoint definition also requires correction to serious adverse events through day 60, as supported by the quoted safety results; confirmation applies specifically to the served harm outcome.
